_about: GM plan and position. Never rendered. Prose for beats, quests and roads lives in saga/bible/_gm/arc.md (saga.py arc <id>); this file holds state. Edit through saga.py plan where a command exists; otherwise with Edit, keeping the canonical format (saga.py fmt).
book_question: Who is hollowing the wounded, and can a knight who cannot stand protect anyone?

chapter.question: What is under the House, and who will take him down to it?

slots.plan: The dawn after the eve, the stair asked for at the door (ch02 choice, option 1). The kitchen's flour at the undercroft door read at the dawn bell before the House can crowd it: no print in or out, a half-moon of frost glazed from the gap, the grains combed toward the door; Sister Pell came down between every bell and heard nothing. The cold comes up nightly, alone. The House wants the door off its pins today; Darrow holds it to the Mender's count and the Prior's key. The first day of asking: Maelis asks the Prior's question first, and his answer (come back up, on this leg) is right and not yet true.
slots.turn: By the end the House knows the cold comes up every night, alone, and is held to the Mender's count and the Prior's key; Darrow has an answer to the Prior's question that is right but not yet true; he attempts to read the flour before anyone steps in it and to keep the House from the door without the Prior's word

slots.plan: q1.letters compressed (stages 2 and 3, arc q1.letters), moved up to Monday so the stair can follow the Knot. At the hour bell Marrant comes up to the bars himself with two letters in blue wax and hands them through, courteous, as if he were the House's carrier. The second: 'Did you turn? Tell me you did not turn toward the boy.' The third, folded inside it: 'Answer me, or I will come myself.' The second is dated before the list was read at Coldmere: Aldric has known where he is all along. Marrant thanks him for taking them and asks nothing about the undercroft, which he has not heard of. Hollis, at the post or the Grey Cot, sees the blue wax a second time and looks away (T3 plant). No asking of the Mender on the page beyond one line of Wren's count, if any. Ends on the micro.
slots.turn: By the end Darrow knows his oldest friend has known where he lay since before the list, and must answer him, burn him, or keep him; he attempts to take the letters from the Confessor's hand without giving the Confessor his face

micro.ask: What does Darrow do with his brother's letters?
options: Write back as a brother: he will not kneel, and why
Burn them, as he burned the first
Keep them, folded, under the mattress

slots.plan: Opens with Wren on the gate wall with Pell's glass reporting riders far down the Holloway under a banner that is not grey (q1.letters stage 3's end; they do not arrive this chapter). Then the Knot (Knot III, the leg bears his weight: a stair with a hand on the wall): Maelis's reading finds it tied, and the leg proves it on the nine steps to the warming room, her counting, his hand on the wall; nine down, nine up, nothing paid but pride. On the top step she gives her first unforced yes, in her own words and not as a bargain (c02.16a). He goes straight to the Prior with the answer to her question, true now: he will come back up it, on this leg, at the Mender's count. At dusk Mother Ione takes the key from her neck and turns it, the first Prior to do so, with the House kept back at the far end; the door opens on the stair and the cold comes up it to meet them. Ends on the first step down.
slots.turn: By the end the leg has borne him on a stair, the Mender has said yes, and the Prior has opened the door: the stair is his to take; he attempts the warming-room steps without the hand on the wall, and Maelis puts it back

slots.plan: The descent (arc b1.3, plants; option 1): Wren first with the lamp and his hand on her shoulder, Maelis behind them without a lamp, counting; Hollis carried to the stair's head, his voice from the top telling him to look at the wall and not the floor; every step down a negotiation (texture, never a stake). Wren counts the steps. At the bottom a hall older than the House, cut and painted: Wren reads the words cut over the inner door aloud before Maelis can translate them, and stops herself halfway (T6); murals of the Reckoning on the walls, and among them a kneeling knight with light running up out of him along a thread (T7 plant). Maelis walks the dark as if she had a lamp. They come back up the same way, the cold on their backs.
slots.turn: By the end Darrow has gone down the stair and come back up it on his own leg, and has seen a Warden hall under the House that nobody living walks but one; he attempts to read the walls, and Wren reads the door first

slots.plan: q1.cart compressed (stages 2 and 3, arc q1.cart): the cage comes up light, a load the grey cloaks have 'inspected'; Rae and Wren on the rope at the top, Rae's palms showing what the rope has done to them. Unasked, Rae says what the almoner's satchel weighed going down last week and what it weighed coming up (b1.2's clue; nobody knows yet what it means). Then the only thing she has ever brought up the mountain that was not on a manifest: the grey mare is alive, lame, a Holloway dealer's, and can be had for the dealer's debt (thread 15). Ends on the micro. The dusk bell catches her at the top and the House keeps her as a guest; on the gate wall at night, the camp's fires below, he tells her what the frost does on the stone under the House, and she tells him at last about the cold in her cart: a crate she once carried to Calden's lower door that froze her cart-bed in midsummer; she does not know what was in it, and she asks him nothing.
slots.turn: By the end Darrow knows the grey mare lives and must say what he will send down for her, and has Rae's cold at last without knowing what it means; he attempts to keep his face for the mare in front of Wren

micro.ask: The mare can be had for the dealer's debt. What does Darrow send down?
options: His name, as surety: a captain's word, though the Faithless have no credit in the Lowmarch
Word, through Rae, that the mare is wanted for the House's stables, in Mother Ione's name
Nothing. Leave her where she is

slots.plan: Back down, deeper: the frost has a direction. With the lamp, Wren's shoulder and Maelis's count, they follow it along the floor of the Warden hall and past a door with script round its frame and no handle, where Maelis's hand rests a moment too long (q1.door). The frost thickens toward the east, under where the infirmary floor must be above them, and ends at a low alcove in the wall, rimed white, too cold to stand near for long: mortar around something, the mortar new. Maelis will not let him touch it today. They come up with the measure of it, and with what they will need: a lamp, oilcloth, a pry bar from the kitchen.
slots.turn: By the end Darrow knows where the cold comes from, a thing set in new mortar under the hall, and that someone put it there; he attempts to touch it and Maelis stops him

slots.plan: The eve of the climax. Above, the House holds its breath: the far cots, the Grey Cot, the lad's frost; Hollis at the stair's head again. Below, the three of them go down with the lamp, the oilcloth and the kitchen's pry bar to the alcove, and Darrow sets the bar to the new mortar. Ends there: the climax is what comes out of it, and what it costs.
slots.turn: By the end Darrow is at the alcove with the bar set to the mortar, the House above waiting; he attempts to do it himself rather than let Wren or Maelis take the cold

world_moves: the grey cloaks built a stone windbreak on the lower terrace and roofed it with the camp's cart-canvas: they mean to winter
a lymer came up to the Confessors' camp from the valley; its baying comes up the Steps after dark and the House's kennel answers it
the first hard frost took the last herbs in the cloister garden, and the kitchen opened the winter stores a week early

climax.plan: What is under the House (arc b1.3). The alcove beneath the infirmary floor, the frost spreading from it, and in it a sliver of the same black stone as the chip under Benedek's tongue, set in mortar that is new, laid since the first snow, in a hole the width of a letter-satchel; the cold drawing up through the floor toward the wounded above (`shard_found`). The murals around them: the Reckoning, and among them a kneeling knight with light running up out of him along a thread (T7 plant; a new thread). By tier: Triumph, Darrow reads the murals aloud as far as the Reckoning lets him and brings the shard up wrapped in oilcloth, the frost burning through to his hands, and on the far cots the Hollowed turn their heads to follow it; Hard-won, the shard is too cold to lift and stays, but he has seen it and the fresh mortar, and that is enough to know it was carried; Costly, the shard is gone when they come back with the lamp and Maelis, the mortar still wet: someone in the House moved it between dusk and dawn; Setback, the alcove is empty and newly broken, and at dusk Marrant announces at the bars that he will inspect the undercroft for witchery under his writ. Hollis waits at the stair's head and is the first face when they come up. The knee is never the stake: the stair back up is texture. Ends on the choice: who is told.
checks: insight DC 13 (Warden's Eye: the mortar's age, the murals, what was carried and how)
vigor DC 13 (holding the cold of the stone long enough: the frost into his hands)
finesse DC 12 (freeing the shard from the mortar without breaking it)
options: Tell the Prior everything, shard and murals
Tell Hollis and the far cots' keepers first, and the Prior only after: his own people before the House's law
Tell no one yet, and watch the stair

ysra.note: the Needle of Calden; Book II; a companion only if spared and if she comes over (q3.needle); approval banks here until then

ilse.note: the red-handed woman, unnamed on the page until b3.2; Book III; approval banks here until she arrives

quest_summary: Confessor Ivo Marrant is coming up the Holloway with five grey cloaks (six in all), a cart, a censer, and a writ naming the Faithless at Saint Ysolde's. Darrow's name is first; Hollis is second. Rae Thorne, the carter who heard the list read, is in the House; her cart and oxen wait at the winch-house below, where one of the six will stay; the rest camp on the lower terrace under the gate.
